full_text_en:
Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd. et al. v. Gansu Aizhitai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a contract for cooperative real estate development

Ruling Summary

In a bilateral contract where both parties have breached their obligations, the determination of whether a party is entitled to rescind the contract shall be made based on a comprehensive assessment of factors including the allocation of contractual duties, the degree of performance of the contract, and the extent of each party's breach.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 126

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Gansu Aizhitai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 301, No. 258 Qingyang Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Dou Yibo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Xing Guoguang, Attorney at Beijing Han Ding Lian He Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiaoyu, Attorney at Gansu Yongsheng Law Firm.

Appellees (Plaintiffs at First Instance): Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 6 Tianshui North Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Song Zushan, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Yan Tianbin, Attorney at Gansu Herui Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ligong, Attorney at Gansu Herui Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Gansu Province Nongken Electromechanical General Company, domiciled at No. 300 Tanjianzi, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Kegong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yan Tianbin, Attorney at Gansu Herui Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ligong, Attorney at Gansu Herui Law Firm.

The appellant, Gansu Aizhitai Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aizhitai Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2010) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 rendered on June 1, 2012, by the Gansu High People's Court in the case concerning a dispute over a joint venture and cooperative real estate development contract with the appellees, Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yongchang Trading Company) and Gansu Province Nongken Electromechanical General Company (hereinafter referred to as Nongken Electromechanical Company). This Court, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on December 14, 2012. The agents ad litem of Aizhitai Company, Xing Guoguang and Zhang Xiaoyu, and the agents ad litem of Yongchang Trading Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company, Yan Tianbin and Wang Ligong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded upon review.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

On December 11, 2006, Aizhitai Company, Yongchang Trading Company, and Nongken Electromechanical Company entered into a Joint Development Cooperation Agreement stipulating the following: Aizhitai Company and Yongchang Trading Company had signed a joint development cooperation agreement in November 2001 to jointly develop and construct the Yinyin Building project. Pursuant to that agreement, Yongchang Trading Company was obligated to handle the land transfer of the jointly developed project land to Aizhitai Company. In order to expedite the land transfer of the parcel at No. 489 Tanjianzi, to facilitate the smooth development and construction of the jointly developed Yinyin Building project, and to further clarify the rights and obligations of the three parties, the following clauses were specially stipulated:

I. Overview of the Yinyin Building Project. The total floor area of the Yinyin Building project is 49,586.14 square meters (excluding the civil air defense level). The project under this contract is a jointly developed project, and each party shall fulfill its respective obligations for the success of the project. The project establishment, planning, construction, and sales shall be conducted in the name of Aizhitai Company.

II. Division of Benefits: 1. Between Aizhitai Company and Yongchang Trading Company. According to the area division agreement dated December 15, 2005, the division is as follows: Aizhitai Company shall receive 65% of the jointly divided area (axes (1)-(2)) from the first to the twenty-eighth floor to which both Aizhitai Company and Yongchang Trading Company are entitled, and Yongchang Trading Company shall receive 35%. 2. Between Aizhitai Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company. The total area to be distributed between Aizhitai Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company: According to the area division agreement dated January 12, 2006, the division is as follows: Aizhitai Company shall receive 65% of the jointly divided area (axes (3)-(4)) to which both Aizhitai Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company are entitled, and Nongken Electromechanical Company shall receive 35%, specifically for the first to twenty-eighth floors of the Yinyin Building, Aizhitai Company shall receive 65% and Nongken Electromechanical Company shall receive 35%.

III. Responsibilities of the Three Parties. The three parties shall abide by and perform the aforementioned area division agreement. After Yongchang Trading Company completes the land transfer, Aizhitai Company shall not mortgage, guarantee, contribute as capital in shares, or sell the real property of the areas allocated to Yongchang Trading Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company. Within three working days after the signing of this agreement, Yongchang Trading Company shall fulfill the commitment clause contained in the agreement signed with Aizhitai Company on December 15, 2005, which stipulated that "the land use right of 5.019 mu for the construction area of the Yinyin Building, as recorded in the land certificate, shall be immediately transferred to Aizhitai Company," and shall provide all documents, certificates, and related applications necessary for the transfer.

On December 22, the three parties signed a supplemental agreement stipulating: 1. The Yinyin Building construction project is a jointly developed project among the three parties; 2. The land occupied by the current joint development construction project is 5.019 mu. Although it was previously a land parcel held under the land use right in the name of Yongchang Trading Company, approximately 2.33 mu of this land is actually used by Nongken Electromechanical Company and serves as the basis for its participation in the joint development and division; 3. Aizhitai Company shall be responsible for handling all procedures for the property certificates of the three parties, with each party bearing its own costs; 4. For the demolition of the Yantan Tax Office, Supply and Marketing Company, and Township Seed Station on the land occupied by the joint development project, Yongchang Trading Company shall allocate properties to these units from its share by the end of October 2007. If the properties cannot be delivered upon expiration of this deadline, the deferred transition fee for the delayed delivery shall be calculated according to the demolition transition fee quota in effect at the time of demolition, and shall be borne by Aizhitai Company and its construction unit. If the common areas in the Yinyin Building that are not subject to the three-party distribution are actually put into operation, the resulting operating revenue and related liabilities shall be distributed by the actual operator according to the proportion of the three parties' building shares; 5. The buildings allocated to each party in proportion must be published in the sales department of Aizhitai Company. At the same time, the actual buildings allocated to the three parties shall be determined on the construction floor plan, confirmed by the three parties by affixing their seals on the drawing, and retained by each party for reference upon delivery; 6. Nongken Electromechanical Company must, upon delivery of the buildings, repay the demolition compensation borrowed from the City Infrastructure Investment Company under the guarantee of Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company. If it fails to repay on time, Yongchang Trading Company or Aizhitai Company shall make the repayment, and the properties allocated to Nongken Electromechanical Company shall then belong to the party that actually made the repayment.

On December 21, 2004, the three parties also signed a meeting minutes regarding Aizhitai Company's request for an early start of construction, which stated: Early start of construction is approved. On February 21, 2006, Aizhitai Company and Zhejiang Hongcheng Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongcheng Company) signed the Yinyin Building Construction Works Agreement, stipulating that Hongcheng Company would undertake the general contract for the construction of the Yinyin Building located at Tanjianzi, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, consisting of two underground floors and twenty-eight above-ground floors with a total construction area of 60,000 square meters. The contract method was labor and partial materials, with a total construction period of 720 calendar days. During the performance of this agreement: 1. Because the Yinyin Building project had not obtained approval from the Lanzhou City Planning Administration Department and had not obtained the relevant four permits, it was subject to administrative penalties by the Lanzhou City Planning Bureau (see Lanzhou City Planning Bureau Decision on Penalty No. 070 (2006) dated September 28, 2006); 2. Aizhitai Company illegally pre-sold some buildings without obtaining a commercial housing pre-sale permit; 3. Because Aizhitai Company failed to pay the project funds as agreed, the project has only completed the main structure to date (see the effective Civil Mediation Letter (2007) Cheng Min San Chu Zi No. 305 of the Chengguan District People's Court of Lanzhou City, Gansu Province; Civil Mediation Letter (2010) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 of the Gansu High People's Court; and Civil Judgment (2010) Gan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 67 of the Gansu High People's Court), thus giving rise to this lawsuit.

The court of first instance also found that according to the facts confirmed in the Civil Judgment (2010) Gan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 67 of the Gansu High People's Court, the cost of the main structure of the Yinyin Building was RMB 44,417,189.76; upon application of Aizhitai Company for appraisal, the upfront costs actually incurred by Aizhitai Company for the project were RMB 14,240,294.04, and the overdue design fees were RMB 2,192,800, totaling RMB 60,850,283.80. The parties raised no objection to the appraisal conclusion upon cross-examination, so it should be accepted. Additionally, according to the Civil Mediation Letter (2010) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 of the Gansu High People's Court, Aizhitai Company was required to pay Gansu Tianqi Material Group Co., Ltd. more than RMB 86 million for steel, cement, and other materials by June 30, 2010. This case is currently under enforcement. Due to Aizhitai Company's breach, its construction works contract with Hongcheng Company was rescinded (see Civil Judgment (2010) Gan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 67). Furthermore, according to the Enforcement Report of the Lanzhou Railway Transportation Intermediate People's Court on the Case of Dispute over Outstanding Payment for Goods Between Lanzhou Tianqi Material Group Co., Ltd. and Aizhitai Company, because Aizhitai Company lacks the ability to repay its debts, creditors have applied to the court for appraisal and auction of the Yinyin Building.

The court of first instance further found the following:

1. On July 18 and August 5, 2001, Nongken Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company signed a Joint Development Cooperation Agreement and a Joint Development Supplemental Agreement regarding the transfer and development of Nongken Electromechanical Company's land located at No. 489 Tanjianzi, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City (its office, business, and residential site). On August 4, 2001, Nongken Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company signed a meeting minutes for a supplemental agreement, the main content being: to apply for construction project establishment and obtain the remaining four permits (excluding the land use permit) including the planning permit in the name of Aizhitai Company, and to handle the division of property certificates for both parties' assets. On November 21, 2001, and October 10, 2003, the parties further signed joint development supplementary agreements on matters such as joint development area, compensation and resettlement, completion date, and distribution of residential, office, and commercial buildings. On January 12, 2006, Nongken Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company signed another agreement on the proportion of profit division. 2. On November 21, 2001, Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company signed a joint development cooperation agreement, agreeing to jointly develop and construct a 3,970 square meter site belonging to Yongchang Trading Company at No. 489 Tanjianzi, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City. On December 15, 2005, the parties signed an agreement on the division of the area of the Yinyin Building based on the aforementioned agreement clauses. 3. On October 11, 2006, Lanzhou City Infrastructure Investment Company (hereinafter referred to as the City Infrastructure Company), Yongchang Trading Company, Nongken Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company signed a four-party agreement. It stipulated: (1) Aizhitai Company's demolition compensation of RMB 6.64 million payable to Nongken Electromechanical Company was temporarily advanced by the City Infrastructure Company; (2) Within 10 days after the effective date of this agreement, Nongken Electromechanical Company shall complete its relocation, and Aizhitai Company shall complete the demolition and removal of construction waste within 20 days after Nongken Electromechanical Company completes its relocation. The compensation advanced by the City Infrastructure Company shall be paid in full within 10 days after the effective date of this agreement; (3) Within 12 months after the signing of this agreement, Aizhitai Company shall provide in-kind resettlement to Nongken Electromechanical Company in the jointly developed Yinyin Building project with Yongchang Trading Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company. The specific resettlement standards shall be as set out in the Resettlement Compensation Agreement and the Joint Development Agreement signed between Yongchang Trading Company, Nongken Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company; (4) After Aizhitai Company provides in-kind resettlement to Nongken Electromechanical Company, or on the corresponding day 12 months after the signing of this agreement, Nongken Electromechanical Company shall repay the demolition compensation advanced by the City Infrastructure Company in a lump sum. If Nongken Electromechanical Company fails to repay on time, it shall pay a penalty to the City Infrastructure Company at a daily rate of 0.04% of the total compensation for each day of delay, with Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company assuming joint and several liability; (5) For this agreement, Nongken Electromechanical Company shall provide a mortgage guarantee using the real estate of the Yinyin Building under construction by Aizhitai Company. If Nongken Electromechanical Company fails to repay the demolition compensation advanced by the City Infrastructure Company on the corresponding day 12 months after the signing of this agreement, the entire Yinyin Building under construction and its land use right shall serve as collateral, and Aizhitai Company and Yongchang Trading Company shall assume joint and several liability; (6) If the Yinyin Building project cannot be delivered for use by October 20, 2007, Aizhitai Company shall unconditionally repay the full amount of the demolition compensation advanced by the City Infrastructure Company and used by Nongken Electromechanical Company. If, upon building delivery, Nongken Electromechanical Company cannot repay the compensation in full to the City Infrastructure Company, then Aizhitai Company shall repay the compensation in full to the City Infrastructure Company, and Nongken Electromechanical Company shall unconditionally withdraw from the project; (7) If a dispute arises due to Aizhitai Company's failure to timely resettle Nongken Electromechanical Company, Nongken Electromechanical Company shall assert its rights against Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company in accordance with the Resettlement Compensation Agreement and the Joint Development Agreement signed with Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company, and the City Infrastructure Company shall not be involved. On October 30, 2007, Nongken Electromechanical Company sent a letter to the City Infrastructure Company stating: Your company, my company, Yongchang Trading Company, and Aizhitai Company jointly negotiated and signed the four-party agreement on October 20, 2006. As of now, Aizhitai Company has failed to deliver the buildings to us for use on schedule. According to the four-party agreement, Aizhitai Company shall bear full responsibility for repayment.

The court of first instance also found that on March 28, 2002, the Lanzhou Municipal People's Government issued the Notice on the Allocation of Construction Land to Yongchang Trading Company (Lan Zheng Jian Zi (2002) No. 078). On August 31, 2004, the Lanzhou City Planning and Land Resources Bureau signed a contract for the transfer of state-owned land use rights in urban Lanzhou with Yongchang Trading Company. On May 26, 2005, the Lanzhou Municipal People's Government issued a state-owned land use permit to Yongchang Trading Company (Lan Guo Yong (2005) No. C06978) and registered it.

The court of first instance further found that Yongchang Trading Company was originally Lanzhou Tanjianzi Agriculture, Industry and Commerce Enterprise Corporation, affiliated with the Community Residents' Committee of Tanjianzi Village, Tannan Street, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City. On January 9, 2008, it was approved by the Chengguan Branch of the Lanzhou City Administration for Industry and Commerce to change its name to its current name. The Community Residents' Committee of Tanjianzi Village, Tannan Street, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City confirmed that Yongchang Trading Company would bear the legal consequences arising from this lawsuit.

Yongchang Trading Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company filed a complaint, alleging that between July 18, 2001, and December 11, 2006, they entered into multiple Joint Development Cooperation Agreements and Joint Development Supplemental Agreements with Aizhitai Company, pursuant to which they provided 5.019 mu of state-owned land use rights located at No. 489 Tanjianzi, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, and Aizhitai Company provided funds for the cooperative development of the Yinyin Building commercial and residential building. During the performance of the joint development cooperation agreement, Aizhitai Company failed to provide funds, causing the construction of the Yinyin Building to stop. Aizhitai Company failed to deliver the agreed-upon buildings to them as stipulated in the joint development agreement and illegally pre-sold buildings. Aizhitai Company had breached the contract. Therefore, they requested: 1. Rescission of the Joint Development Cooperation Agreement signed by the three parties; 2. Aizhitai Company be ordered to bear liability for breach of contract and compensate for losses in the amount of RMB 121,170,840 (the final amount to be determined by the court's appraisal); 3. The case acceptance fee and appraisal fees be borne by Aizhitai Company.

Aizhitai Company did not submit a written defense. In court, it requested that the contract continue to be performed and that the claims of Yongchang Trading Company and Nongken Electromechanical Company be dismissed.

The court of first instance held that a contract lawfully formed is legally binding upon the parties. The parties shall perform their obligations in accordance with the contract. According to the Joint Construction Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement, Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company invested their transferred land use right of 5.019 mu as capital contribution, and jointly constructed the Yinyin Building with Aizhitai Company as the capital contributor. However, since the joint construction of the building commenced, Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company did not complete the land transfer procedures for Aizhitai Company, resulting in the failure to obtain the necessary permits for construction project approval, planning, construction, and pre-sale, which should have been handled by Aizhitai Company, up to the time of the project's suspension. This caused the under-construction Yinyin Building to become an illegal structure and subject to penalties. Aizhitai Company, as the capital contributor in the joint construction, lacked financial support, causing the project to be shelved for three years after the main structure was topped out, and it had long been in arrears for materials, engineering costs, and workers' wages. Based on the facts confirmed by the effective Civil Mediation Paper of the Gansu Higher People's Court (2010) Gan Min Er Chu Zi No. 12 and the Civil Judgment of the Gansu Higher People's Court (2010) Gan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 67, Aizhitai Company's arrears for engineering and material costs, including interest, had reached over RMB 120 million, making performance of the joint construction contract impossible. The claims of Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company for rescission of the joint construction contract were established and should be supported. Although Yongchang Trading Company, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company were properly qualified as parties to the contract, and the multiple joint construction agreements and supplemental agreements signed by the three parties were formed, Aizhitai Company, as the capital contributor in the joint construction, first, had entered into a construction project construction contract with Hongcheng Company before the tripartite agreement was signed, and by the time the contract was rescinded, it had not yet obtained the necessary permits for construction project approval, planning, construction, and pre-sale. Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company also did not timely complete the land transfer or assist Aizhitai Company in handling other procedures. Both parties were in breach of contract, and the expected benefits of each party could not be realized. Second, Aizhitai Company illegally sold houses without obtaining planning and pre-sale permits and did not use the pre-sale proceeds for the under-construction project. The fault liability for this should be borne by Aizhitai Company itself. Third, Aizhitai Company did not pay the engineering costs as agreed in the contract, causing the project to be suspended to date, and it still owed Hongcheng Company engineering costs of RMB 15,126,810.57. Since both parties violated the contract terms, the claim of Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company for damages for breach of contract in the amount of RMB 121,170,840 (allocable area of 20,195.14 sqm multiplied by the estimated average market price of RMB 6,000/sqm at the time of the lawsuit) was not supported. Aizhitai Company demonstrated through its own conduct that it could not perform its contractual obligations and did not file a counterclaim, so its claim for continued performance of the contract was also not supported. In summary, the court of first instance ruled: (1) The Joint Construction Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement signed by Yongchang Trading Company, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company were terminated. (2) Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company shall pay Aizhitai Company a total of RMB 60,850,283.80, based on Aizhitai Company's actual investment in the completed works of the Yinyin Building (main structure cost of RMB 44,417,189.76 + Aizhitai Company's initial investment expenses of RMB 14,240,294.04 + overdue design fees of RMB 2,192,800), and shall pay interest on Aizhitai Company's initial investment expenses (calculated in installments based on the order of payment) and interest on the main structure cost (calculated in installments based on the amounts paid from February 2006) at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, up to the time the lawsuit was filed. (3) Within 30 days after the judgment takes effect, after Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company pay Aizhitai Company the actual investment costs and interest, Aizhitai Company shall hand over the construction site to Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company. (4) The claims of Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company for Aizhitai Company to bear losses for breach of contract were dismissed. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 647,654 and the appraisal fee of RMB 233,900, totaling RMB 881,554, shall be borne equally by Yongchang Trading Company, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company, each paying RMB 440,777. If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Aizhitai Company was dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance and appealed to this Court.

Aizhitai Company appealed, arguing: (1) The original judgment terminating the Joint Construction Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement had no legal basis. The land and original office building owned by Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company had never undergone any planning procedures and were illegal structures, which prevented the completion of related land development and construction procedures. Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company had no lawful right to use the land in question and was not a proper party to this case. Aizhitai Company committed no breach of contract. Yongchang Trading Company failed to complete the land use right transfer procedures as agreed and should bear all liability for breach. (2) The original judgment's determination of the engineering costs and quantity of work was inconsistent with the facts. The RMB 44 million was only the cost of the main civil works completed by the construction party, not the total cost of all completed works in the project. The construction and materials for related structures and structural components other than the building's main body were completed by Aizhitai Company itself, and the volume of that work was not included. The first-instance judgment found that Aizhitai Company owed over RMB 80 million in material costs to Gansu Tianqi Materials Group Co., Ltd., yet only found Aizhitai Company's total investment to be over RMB 60 million, which was contradictory. (3) The lawsuit between Aizhitai Company and the construction party Hongcheng Company was due to the construction party's failure to complete the project according to the schedule agreed in the construction contract. The project suspension was not due to Aizhitai Company's lack of financial support, but because Yongchang Trading Company intentionally obstructed it. Accordingly, the appeal requested: 1. To set aside items (1), (2), and (3) of the first-instance judgment; 2. To rule that Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company's qualification and standing as a party to the joint construction be revoked, and that Yongchang Trading Company and Aizhitai Company continue to perform the joint construction agreement; 3. That all first-instance and second-instance litigation costs, appraisal fees, etc., be borne by Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company.

Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company responded, arguing that Aizhitai Company failed to invest funds as agreed, which prevented it from achieving the purpose of the joint construction contract within the contractually agreed period and led to years of disputes. Aizhitai Company was clearly in breach of contract. The original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly. They requested the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

During the second-instance trial, all parties acknowledged that the main structure of the project in question had been completed.

This Court also found that, in the case of Aizhitai Company v. Hongcheng Company concerning a general construction project contract dispute, the Gansu Higher People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2010) Gan Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 67 on January 4, 2011, which has now become effective. That judgment found that in June 2008, Hongcheng Company was forced to suspend work because Aizhitai Company failed to pay progress payments and purchase necessary materials as agreed. Aizhitai Company filed that lawsuit on the grounds that Hongcheng Company's unjustified suspension caused it economic losses.

Other facts found in the second-instance trial are consistent with those found in the first-instance trial.

This Court holds that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company have the statutory right to rescind the Joint Construction Agreement and the Supplemental Agreement. Aizhitai Company argued that Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company lacked the standing to be a party to the Joint Construction Agreement. Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company claimed that Aizhitai Company principally committed two breaches: first, it failed to complete the procedures for project registration, planning, construction, and pre-sale for the joint construction project, resulting in the project becoming an illegal structure and subject to penalties; second, it failed to deliver the joint construction property on time.

Regarding whether Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company has the standing to be a party to the Joint Construction Agreement. According to the facts found in the first-instance trial, on July 18, 2001, August 5, 2001, November 21, 2001, October 10, 2003, January 12, 2006, December 11, 2006, and December 22, 2006, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company signed multiple joint construction cooperation agreements and supplemental agreements. Aizhitai Company acknowledged the authenticity and validity of each joint construction agreement it signed with Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company. According to Article 8, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the PRC, a lawfully formed contract is protected by law. Therefore, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company is a contractual party to the multiple joint construction agreements and supplemental agreements in question, and its contractual rights should be protected by law. Article 2 of the supplemental agreement signed by Yongchang Trading Company, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company on December 22, 2006, stipulated: "The joint construction development project currently occupies 5.019 mu of land. Although the land parcel was previously in the name of Yongchang Trading Company's land use right, approximately 2.33 mu of the land is actually used by Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company and serves as the basis for its participation in the distribution of the joint construction." It can be seen from the above that, although the land use right for the land in question was registered in the name of Yongchang Trading Company, the parties were aware of the true ownership status of the land. The contract terms were also clear, and these terms did not violate the provisions of the law. Therefore, the above agreement is binding on all parties. Even assuming that Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company had no right to dispose of the subject matter, this would not affect the validity of the joint construction agreements or supplemental agreements, and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company would still enjoy the relevant contractual rights. In summary, Aizhitai Company's argument that Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company lacked the standing to be a joint construction party because it had no rights or interests in the land in question is untenable.

Regarding the failure to complete the project registration and planning procedures. According to the facts already found, Article 3 of the Joint Construction Supplemental Agreement signed between Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company in May 2001 stipulated that the project registration and project initiation should be carried out in Aizhitai Company's name, all fees were to be borne and paid by Aizhitai Company, and with the exception that the land use certificate would still be obtained in the name of Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company in the early stages of the project, the other four certificates were to be applied for and obtained in Aizhitai Company's name during the registration and initiation process. Article 1, paragraph 4 of the Joint Construction Cooperation Agreement signed between Tanjianzi Agricultural, Industrial and Commercial Enterprise General Company and Aizhitai Company on November 21, 2001, stipulated that Aizhitai Company was responsible for all construction approval work, construction and design, and technical evaluation, until all procedures for commencement were completed (planning land use permit, planning construction permit, construction permit), with all required expenses borne by Aizhitai Company, so that conditions for construction commencement were met. Article 2, paragraph 3 stipulated that Tanjianzi Agricultural, Industrial and Commercial Enterprise General Company had the obligation to cooperate with Aizhitai Company in providing all land documents and related procedures required for the project approval. The Administrative Penalty Decision of the Lanzhou Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, Market Management Second Branch, recorded Aizhitai Company's statement: "The reason the planning procedures were not completed is that the original Lanzhou Tanjianzi Agricultural and Industrial Commercial General Company, represented by the YanTan Furniture Market, had never lawfully completed construction planning procedures for any of its approximate 100 or more development and construction projects. For this reason, the Lanzhou Municipal Planning Bureau delayed the planning and construction procedures for the Yinyin Building until today, on the grounds that the company must first complete the planning procedures for its previous projects before new projects starting after 2005 could be processed." From the above facts, it can be seen that all parties had certain obligations to fulfill regarding the approval procedures for the joint construction project. None of the parties provided sufficient evidence to prove they had fulfilled their respective obligations. Therefore, the failure to effectively complete the planning procedures for the project in question was a responsibility shared by all parties. According to the facts found in the first-instance trial, on December 21, 2004, the three signatory parties signed a meeting minutes concerning Aizhitai Company's request to commence work first. The minutes stated: approval to commence work first. This also indicates that the parties had reached an agreement on commencing work while processing the relevant procedures. Item 2 of the Lanzhou Municipal Planning Bureau's "Administrative Penalty Decision on Illegal Construction Cases" (Lan Gui Jian [2006] No. 070) dated June 28, 2006, stated: "Order to complete the construction project planning procedures retroactively." Based on the planning bureau's penalty decision, the project in question was not a fundamentally illegal structure but rather a project for which construction planning procedures could be retroactively completed. In summary, completing the various planning procedures for the project in question was a joint obligation of the three joint construction parties. Aizhitai Company was responsible for handling the procedures, and Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company were responsible for assisting. All parties bore some responsibility for the failure to complete the planning procedures. Furthermore, all parties were aware of and agreed to the approach of commencing work first and completing the procedures later. At the same time, according to the decision of the relevant administrative department, the project in question was not a fundamentally illegal structure and could be legalized through retroactive completion of the relevant planning procedures. Therefore, although Aizhitai Company failed to successfully complete the planning procedures, this did not constitute a fundamental breach that made it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract. The original judgment, which found that Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company had the right to rescind the contract on the grounds that Aizhitai Company's failure to complete the planning procedures rendered the project an illegal structure, had no factual or legal basis.

Regarding Aizhitai Company's failure to deliver the joint construction property on time. Article 1 of the Joint Construction Supplemental Agreement signed between Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company and Aizhitai Company on October 10, 2003, stipulated that because the demolition of the family apartment building concerned the compensation and resettlement of the relocated households, Aizhitai Company should complete the entire project within 30 months from the date of signing this agreement and deliver the agreed area for use by Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company. If delivery was not made on time, Aizhitai Company should bear the resettlement costs for the relocates of Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company. If Aizhitai Company could not complete the building construction within 36 months, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company would deem Aizhitai Company in breach. Aizhitai Company should then bear all losses of Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company (such as losses caused by the demolition of the building). Article 14 of the Agreement signed between Aizhitai Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company on January 12, 2006, stipulated that Aizhitai Company's construction period would commence from February 20, 2006, and the construction period should not exceed 30 months. If the construction period was exceeded, the liquidated damages would be RMB 30,000 per month. On October 11, 2006, a four-party agreement signed by City Construction Company, Yongchang Trading Company, Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company, and Aizhitai Company stipulated that if the Yinyin Building project could not be delivered for use by October 20, 2007, the demolition compensation costs advanced by City Construction Company for Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company would be unconditionally repaid in full by Aizhitai Company. From the above contract terms, it can be seen that there was no particularly strict time requirement for the delivery of the joint construction property among the parties. The delivery date had been subject to change, and there was no agreement providing for contract rescission due to late delivery. Furthermore, by 2008, the main structure of the project in question was already completed. Therefore, although Aizhitai Company had delayed performance of its obligation, it had not reached the severity of making it impossible to achieve the purpose of the contract. During the period from 2009 to 2011, Aizhitai Company was in litigation with the construction party Hongcheng Company, and the first-instance trial of this case was also suspended due to that litigation. Therefore, the claim that the project in question was suspended for more than three years because Aizhitai Company lacked subsequent funds for performance lacks sufficient factual basis. The facts that Aizhitai Company owed engineering costs and other material costs relate to a different legal relationship from this case and cannot be used to conclude that Aizhitai Company indicated through its own conduct that it would not perform its contractual obligations. While the original judgment found Aizhitai Company in breach, it also found that Yongchang Trading Company had failed to transfer the land in question to Aizhitai Company's name as agreed, constituting a breach of contract. This Court holds that, in a bilateral contract where both parties are in breach, the question of whether a party is entitled to rescind the contract should be considered comprehensively, based on the allocation of contractual obligations, the degree of contract performance, and the extent of each party's breach. Considering the entire case, Aizhitai Company undertook the main work in the joint construction project and had already performed most of its contractual obligations. The main structure of the project in question had been completed. Given that all parties were in breach, finding that Yongchang Trading Company and Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical Company had the statutory right to rescind the contract has no factual or legal basis and would lead to a significant imbalance in the interests of the contracting parties. The original judgment's rescission of the contract was improper, and this Court corrects it. At the same time, according to Article 112 of the Contract Law of the PRC, if one party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, and after performing the obligations or taking remedial measures, the other party still suffers other losses, compensation for losses shall be paid. Therefore, continued performance of the contract does not affect the right of any party to claim liability for breach of contract from the other party.

In summary, according to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment of the Gansu Higher People's Court (2010) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 is set aside;

2. The claims of Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd. and Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical General Company are dismissed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 647,654 and the appraisal fee of RMB 233,900, totaling RMB 881,554, shall be borne by Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd. and Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical General Company, each paying RMB 440,777. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 647,654 shall be borne by Lanzhou Tanjianzi Yongchang Trading Co., Ltd. and Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation Electromechanical General Company, each paying RMB 323,827.

This judgment is final.
